deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematical derivation on this folio. It is a pencil sketch on squared paper. It shows a street plan with a road running roughly from the lower left to the right, lined with a row of rectangular plots or blocks along its northern side, some marked with small hatched building symbols. A curved double-lined path (a road or track) branches off near the lower centre and runs north-north-east, and another path heads to the lower right. Small buildings appear at the lower-left junction. Pencil crosses are drawn at regular intervals over the sheet: a vertical column in the upper middle, a horizontal row near the top right, and a lattice in the lower half. They look like the intersection marks of a rectangular coordinate grid laid out for plotting surveyed points. This is consistent with Gauss's geodetic and cadastral work, such as the Hanoverian triangulation or local plans of Göttingen. On that reading the page would be a field or plotting sketch locating streets and buildings relative to grid lines. The locality cannot be identified from the image, and no coordinates or numbers are legible beyond a few tiny letter or number labels next to features. Nothing here connects to the numerical least-squares and triangulation-type reductions on the previous page (logarithms, angle combinations α+δ, β+γ+ζ, and so on) or to the curve figures on the next page. At most there is a general thematic link to geodesy. No mathematical content can be reconstructed.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains only a map sketch with grid crosses. Gauss's extensive surveying and geodetic mapping work is well known, and the sheet has no mathematical content.
